1.1.support: randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the EPM-guided group or the conventional group using computer-generated randomization

1.2.support: An independent research coordinator, uninvolved in clinical care or outcome assessment, performed the allocation using sequentially numbered, opaque, sealed envelopes

1.3.support: there were no significant differences in baseline characteristics, such as age, sex, body mass index (BMI), comorbidities, APACHE II score, and SOFA score, between the two groups (all p > 0.05)

2.1.support: Patients were sedated, mechanically ventilated ICU patients, and the report gives no indication that patients were aware of their assigned ventilation strategy.

2.2.support: Given the nature of the intervention, blinding of treating physicians was not feasible.

2.3.support: Standardized protocols were followed in both groups, no crossover was permitted, and no deviations from the assigned strategy are reported; there is no evidence the trial context caused protocol deviations.

2.4.support: Answered NA because 2.3 was not Y/PY.

2.6.support: A total of 124 patients with SAP-related ARDS completed the study, including 70 males and 54 females

3.1.support: A total of 124 patients with SAP-related ARDS completed the study ... (n = 62) ... (n = 62); all 124 randomized patients appear in the outcome tables with no reported losses.

4.2.support: Mortality was ascertained identically in both groups over the same 28-day follow-up; no differential ascertainment is reported.

4.3.support: Outcome assessors remained blinded to group allocation throughout the study.

5.1.support: I looked for a trial protocol, statistical analysis plan, or registry record describing pre-specified analyses and found none; only the journal article was available.
5.1.location: Whole article; no protocol or registry reference reported

5.2.support: 28-day mortality is a single outcome domain with only one possible measurement, so selection among multiple measurements is not plausible.

5.3.support: I looked for pre-specified analysis intentions and found none; mortality could have been analysed in multiple ways (e.g. adjusted vs unadjusted), and intentions are not reported.

D1.rationale: Computer-generated randomization with adequate envelope-based concealment by an independent coordinator; baseline characteristics balanced, so no concerns about the randomization process.

D2.rationale: Treating physicians were unavoidably unblinded, but no deviations from the intended intervention arising from the trial context were reported, and an ITT-type analysis including all 124 randomized patients was used.

D3.rationale: Outcome data appear available for all 124 randomized patients (62 per group) with no reported missing data or exclusions.

D4.rationale: All-cause 28-day mortality is an objective outcome, measured identically in both groups, with blinded outcome assessors; knowledge of allocation could not plausibly influence its assessment.

D5.rationale: No protocol, registry record or statistical analysis plan was available, so pre-specified analyses cannot be verified (5.1, 5.3 NI). The algorithm would give Some concerns; no direct evidence of result selection, but analysis intentions cannot be checked. This matches the algorithmic judgement.

overall.rationale: Low risk in domains 1-4 but Some concerns in Domain 5 because the absence of a protocol or analysis plan means selective reporting cannot be excluded; no domain is High.
